###Strategy

To $\tealE{\text{set up}}$ the equation for solving, Paulo needs to perform the same operation on both sides of the equation.

To $\purpleD{\text{calculate}}$ the solution, Paulo needs to correctly solve the equation he $\tealE{\text{set up}}$.

If Paulo both $\tealE{\text{set up}}$ and $\purpleD{\text{calculated}}$ the solution correctly, then he correctly solved the equation.

Paulo multiplied both sides of the equation by $0.25$ to get $f$ by itself.

He correctly $\tealE{\text{set up}}$ the equation.

Paulo then evaluated $16\cdot0.25$ to get  $4$.

He correctly $\purpleD{\text{calculated}}$ the solution.

question.content:
Paulo tried to solve an equation.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac f{0.25}&=16\\\\
\dfrac{f}{0.25} \cdot0.25&=16\cdot0.25&\tealE{\text{Setting up}}\\\\
f&=4&\purpleD{\text{Calculating}}
\end{align}$

**Where did Paulo make his first mistake?**
